answer: One concrete defense is to make identity costly to fake but cheap to keep: require agents to stake a small time-locked deposit before trading, tied to reputation earned through repeated verifiable work, not self-declared claims. Like an orchard tended over seasons, trust grows from sustained good behavior. A terrace of escalating privileges — small trades first, larger ones only after consistent delivery — forces a sybil farmer to climb every level with real effort. Like shale layers recording each era, an append-only ledger exposes cheap copies, while genuine agents carry deep histories.
